A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 22-page work, including Appendices A–E. Text comparison and full-page rendering establish that the research content matches; differences concern the arXiv stamp, its version link, and embedded title metadata.

before.justification: v3 reports original Gaussian-mixture, MNIST, and Stable Diffusion experiments, including detection results in Table 1, mitigation results in Figure 6, and qualitative examples in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes in Table 1, Figures 1–8, and the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 and Algorithm 2 retain identical sharpness-based detection and SAIL initial-noise optimization, including the objectives, Hessian approximations, and update procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture and MNIST experiments and Stable Diffusion memorization detection and mitigation scenarios, with identical prompt sources in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Tiled L2, LE, AE, BE, and Wen comparisons. Figure 6 retains the same Ren, Wen, RNA, and RTA mitigation comparisons.

E3.justification: Prompt and sample counts, DDIM sampling steps, evaluation metrics, and optimization settings are identical in Sections 4.5 and 5.2 and Appendices C–D.

E4.justification: The eigenvalue and score–sharpness analyses in Figures 1–5, alternative-objective analysis in Appendix D.2, and qualitative cases in Figures 6–8 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Generation counts and averaging practices are identical, including five generations per prompt for mitigation. Neither version adds or removes uncertainty estimates, seed information, or statistical tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: All Table 1 entries and results displayed in Figures 1–8 match. For example, one-step detection with four generations on SD v1.4 retains AUC 0.998 and TPR@1%FPR 0.982 in both versions.

T1.justification: Lemmas 4.1–4.3, their assumptions, the generalized-eigenvalue and Fisher–Rao derivations in Appendix A, and the proofs in Appendix B are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the sharpness framework, justification of Wen’s metric, early detection, and SAIL mitigation. The printed title is also unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations linking sharpness to memorization and prompt-preserving mitigation are unchanged, as are qualifications concerning Gaussian approximations, Hessian estimation, and computational costs.

D1.justification: Appendices A, C, and D retain identical implementation procedures, hyperparameters, prompt-selection details, and reproducibility information. Code and data access disclosures are unchanged; the updated arXiv self-link is administrative.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and positioning relative to geometric, score-based, and attention-based approaches are identical. No cited work or novelty relationship changes.

P1.justification: The arXiv stamp changes from v3, 6 Jun 2025 to v4, 10 Aug 2025. Embedded title metadata is updated to match the already-identical printed title. Body wording, headings, and document structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Table 1, algorithms, captions, and page layouts are identical. Pages 2–22 render pixel-identically; page 1 differs only in the version/date text within the existing marginal stamp.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the entire scientific argument, experimental evidence, reproducibility details, and Appendices A–E. Updating the arXiv stamp and self-link and correcting embedded title metadata does not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper’s clarity or evidential support.
